refutation.quote: Code-RL: plain 390, cue 450 (-1.4 vs RL cue [-4.0, 1.0]); Code and Math deltas cos 0.014.
refutation.note: The theory explains result-c9b27e as 'the function lies in the sign pattern, so the two deltas are orthogonal in function', and on that basis claims Code-RL stays near base: t36 412 [393, 428] with the cue and t42 245 [200, 295] plain. Measured: 450 and 390, misses of 38 and 145 right of 500. The study README (studies/rlneurons/README.md, table 'Weight-difference line', from results/day1_wdiff/readout.json) has the same numbers: code_cue 450, code_plain 390, code_cue minus rl_cue -1.4 [-4.0, 1.0]. result-e45bf4 then shows Code-RL equals theta(0.5) on the 328 harder problems: 187 vs 190 of 328, -0.9 [-5.5, 3.7]. A delta with 50.8 % sign agreement buys the same math accuracy as half the Math delta. So whatever buys the accuracy is not specific to the Math delta's sign pattern. The scope names only the Math delta, but the theory chose to explain the Code/Math sign comparison and made claims t36 and t42 itself, so the scope does not exclude it. Neither row counted (the nulls also predicted about 415 and 285), which is why the backtest did not see the miss. Second contradiction: result-d2933e (n=100 screen, rows not in git). The top 8 singular directions per matrix, 9.8 % of the squared norm, score 88/100 plain, against 36 for a random rank-8 subspace (base 34, RL 96). That is a magnitude-ranked subspace that carries far more than its energy share, against 'magnitude-ranked subsets add almost nothing'. Third: result-904bbf, which the theory lists itself as a conflict. Weight-change ranking closes 4.2 % of KL against 0.7 % for random, while holding 1.5 % of the energy.

wins_judgement: The three wins do not support the mechanism. t32 (441 against 440 [428, 452]) and t33 (452 against 452) come from KL closure (1-a)^2 passed through a concave closure-to-accuracy map fitted on the n13 transplant arms. Neither leverage nor signs enter that calculation. Any saturating dose-to-accuracy curve fitted to those arms gives the same two numbers, and the nulls were only 15 and 12 points away (425 and 440). The same map applied to the plain prompt misses (t40), so the cue-row fit is partly luck: the cued gap is small (53 points) and the plateau is wide. t34 (453 at a = 1.5) is a plateau result. r1-surprises-2 predicted the same 450 from 'small delta, linear regime'. The displacement rule (rel dW < 1e-2 is tolerant, 2610.37719 App. E) and 2404.16792 give it too, with no sign coherence needed. The paper's own Olmo-3 RL-Zero-Math (3.0) delta kept only 25 % of its GSM8K gain at 1.5x. Simpler account: accuracy saturates near a = 0.5 for a small delta, and MATH-500's last-answer grading tolerates text that degrades after the answer. The two losses point the same way. t45: word-salad tails are 0-3 for every a <= 1, 14 at a = 1.25 and 34 at a = 1.5 (12 of the 34 still right). So the generated text leaves the linear regime between a = 1 and 1.5, while accuracy holds only because the answer comes before the tail. This is the format drift that 2610.37719 App. E reports, and it refutes 'the dose curve stays near-linear past a = 1' everywhere except the accuracy count. t40: a quarter of the delta takes the plain prompt from 224 to 405, 76 % of the 239-point gap, against the theory's 60 % (360). Only 1 of those 500 answers writes the cue text. The curve is more concave than KL closure allows, which fits a switch that a small dose flips (r1-all-2) better than an effect proportional to energy and leverage.
rival: No theory dominates. All three score 3 wins and 2 losses on the rows that counted. On the cue dose row, r2-across-2 fits best (errors t32 1, t33 0; r1-surprises-2 11 and 6; r1-all-2 26 and 17). On the plain dose row, r1-all-2 fits best (t40 35, t41 11; r2-across-2 45 and 28; r1-surprises-2 95 and 45). On Code-RL, r1-all-2 has the right direction on the plain prompt (315 against 390; r2-across-2 245). Summed absolute error on the 7 accuracy targets that r2-across-2 and r1-all-2 share (t32, t33, t36, t37, t40, t41, t42): r1-all-2 218, r2-across-2 265. r1-all-2 carries one large miss of its own: t06, 3 predicted against 168 measured. r1-surprises-2 is weakest on the plain prompt, but result-d2933e (rank-8 at 88/100) favours its core claim. Separating measurement, plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0, grader v3, 2-3 arms. (i) The top-8-SVD part of each matrix's delta, 9.8 % of the energy. (ii) base + 0.098*(RL - base), the uniform dose with the same projection onto the delta. Optionally (iii) the sign-only delta. Score accuracy and the share of answers that end with the base's 'Answer:' line. r1-surprises-2 predicts (i) much higher than (ii). r2-across-2 predicts (i) about equal to (ii), each closing its share of the coherent pattern, and (iii) at RL level. r1-all-2 predicts that in both arms accuracy follows the boxed-answer share, with a sharp threshold in a.

novelty.nearest: Shiromani 2610.37719, Sec 3 Tables 1-2, App. A Table 9, Sec 7 Eq. 1 / Fig. 5. For allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math minus Olmo-3-1025-7B the paper reports leverage rho_iso 710 on mixed text, 4,356 on math and 235 on WikiText, rho_sign 544 and magnitude alignment 1.59: the effect sits in signs and cross-coordinate structure, and general text moves little. It derives and checks DARE damage = (1-p)/(p*rho_sign) of the delta's own KL, with SFT-like deltas failing by keep 0.1. Code-RL is measured too (rho 388, math 937). The paper reports extrapolation to 1.5x as inconclusive: the 3.0 Math delta kept 25 % of its GSM8K gain, and format drift was seen at 1.5x.
novelty.difference: The paper measures KL on the 3.0 release, tests DARE only on Qwen and OLMo-2-1B deltas, and reports no task accuracy for DARE, sign-flip or sign-only edits on Olmo-3. The theory adds four untested things: the 3.1 MLP delta's flat DARE accuracy from q = 0.1 % to 3 % as a lower bound on leverage of about 1,000-1,500 (above the paper's rho_sign 544), a DARE accuracy cliff at q of about 0.01-0.05 %, a sign-only delta at RL accuracy, and a collapse of the Think-SFT delta under DARE at 1 %.

import_carries_win.which: None. The wins t32 and t33 come from the first-order additivity of result-904bbf plus a fitted concave map; t34 comes from the small-delta argument of 2404.16792. The 2610.37719 import drives only t37, t38 and t47 (random direction is negligible). t37 and t47 landed inside their intervals and t38 missed (42 against 16-34), but none of the three diverged from the nulls, so none counted. The paper's own Olmo-3 RL-Zero-Math data (25 % of the gain kept at 1.5x on GSM8K) would have argued against t34, not for it.

verdict: weak: the three wins follow from a saturating dose curve without leverage or signs, the claims about leverage and signs for these models are already in 2610.37719, and the theory's own inferences fail on the counter-examples it chose (Code-RL 450/390 against its 412/245; word salad rising to 34/500 at a = 1.5). Only the DARE-cliff and sign-only predictions are left to test.
